# DSP Architecture: PRISM

**CRITICAL CONTRACT:** This specification is immutable during Stages 1-3 implementation. Stage 2 (DSP + analysis engine) implements this exact architecture. Changes require an explicit amendment note in section 12.

**Generated by:** Stage 0 Research (research-planning-agent), 2026-10-15
**Referenced by:** Stage 1 (Foundation), Stage 2 (DSP/Analysis), Stage 3 (GUI integration)
**Purpose:** Defines the analysis engine, threading model, snapshot data layout, bus layout, parameter-to-behavior mapping, and test strategy for PRISM.
**Upstream contracts (read-only):** `creative-brief.md`, `parameter-spec.md` (LOCKED, 17 APVTS + 2 state entries + bridge events + Meter Definitions), `mockups/v8-ui.yaml`, `mockups/v8-PluginEditor.h/.cpp`, `mockups/v8-integration-checklist.md`.

---

## 0. What PRISM is, in DSP terms

PRISM is a **zero-latency, bit-exact passthrough** with a side-channel analysis engine. `processBlock()` never writes to any output sample. Its only job is to copy input samples of each source into a lock-free ring and update three cheap atomics. All analysis (FFT, loudness, true peak, stereo metrics, scope/gonio capture, band energies) runs on **one dedicated worker thread**, which publishes **immutable `AnalysisSnapshot`s** that the editor's 60 Hz timer fetches and forwards to the WebView as `prismFrame`.

None of the 17 APVTS parameters affect the audio path or the measurements' meaning (exceptions listed in section 4: `fft_size`, `window`, `analysis_mode` select *which analysis is computed*; they never alter audio).

---

## Core Components

### C1. Source Registry
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (`prism::SourceRegistry`), uses `juce::AudioProcessor::BusesProperties`, `getBusBuffer()`
- **Purpose:** Maps host buses to analysis sources. v1: source 0 = main input bus (index 0), source 1 = sidechain input bus (index 1). Compile-time capacity `kMaxSources = 16`; v1 `kSourceCount = 2` (the constant already used in the v8 `AnalysisSnapshot`).
- **Parameters Affected:** `src1_visible/src1_solo/src2_visible/src2_solo` (display only, pass through the snapshot untouched - never gate analysis); `src1_name/src2_name` (state only)
- **Configuration:**
  - Each source records: `busIndex`, `numChannels` (1 or 2), `active` (bus enabled and layout valid).
  - Per-source analysis objects (C2-C9) are allocated only for active sources in `prepareToPlay`; arrays are sized `kMaxSources` so v2 (Sender IPC sources) and N-bus hosts add entries without touching engine code.
  - Hidden (not visible) sources keep full analysis ("analysis state for hidden sources is still maintained" per spec).

### C2. Audio-thread Capture (the only audio-thread code)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (`prism::SpscFrameRing`), `juce::AbstractFifo` is NOT used (we need frame-contiguous variable-length memcpy with release/acquire semantics and a power-of-two mask; a 40-line custom ring is simpler and provably wait-free)
- **Purpose:** Copy each source's L/R (or mono) samples into a per-source SPSC ring; update lossless peak atomic; record beat events.
- **Parameters Affected:** none
- **Configuration:**
  - Ring: planar-in-one-allocation `float[channels][capacity]`, `capacity = 2^18` frames (1.37 s at 192 kHz, 5.9 s at 44.1 kHz), allocated in `prepareToPlay`. Writer owns `writeIdx` (atomic<uint64>, release-store after the memcpy); reader owns `readIdx` (acquire-load). Overrun policy: if free space < block, **drop the whole block, increment `overrunCount` (relaxed atomic) and continue** - never block, never overwrite unread data. The worker treats an overrun as a discontinuity (see C6/C7 "gap handling").
  - Per block per source: `blockPeak = max|x|` over all channels (one vectorizable pass, NaN/Inf-aware: non-finite samples are counted into `nonFiniteCount` and excluded from the peak); then a single CAS-loop `fetch_max` into `std::atomic<float> samplePeakSinceDrain`. This makes **sample peak lossless even across ring overruns**.
  - Mono bus: ring has 1 channel; the worker treats it as `hasStereo=false`.
  - Host transport: `getPlayHead()->getPosition()` read once per block (`AudioPlayHead::PositionInfo`): `getBpm()` -> `std::atomic<float> bpm` (NaN when absent); if `getIsPlaying()` and `getPpqPosition()`/`getTimeSignature()` are available, compute whether a beat / bar boundary falls inside this block and push `{absSampleIndex, isBar}` to a tiny SPSC `BeatEventQueue` (capacity 256, drop on full).
  - `ScopedNoDenormals` at the top of `processBlock` (cheap FPU flag; does not modify audio data).
  - **Bit-transparency:** `processBlock` takes `const` views of the buffer; the buffer is never written, cleared, or resized. Sidechain channels (indices >= main channel count in the shared host buffer) are only read.

### C3. Analysis Worker + Engine Scheduler
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::Thread` (subclass `prism::AnalysisWorker`), `juce::WaitableEvent` (only for the worker's own wait/stop, never signalled from the audio thread)
- **Purpose:** Owns all per-source analyzers; drains rings; runs analyzers; publishes snapshots.
- **Parameters Affected:** reads `fft_size`, `window`, `analysis_mode` (raw atomic via `apvts.getRawParameterValue`, safe from any thread)
- **Configuration:**
  - Loop: `drain()` all source rings into per-source `StreamHistory` (C4) -> run continuous analyzers on new frames -> if due, run FFT hops -> if the publish timer elapsed, build + publish a snapshot -> `wait(poll)`.
  - Poll interval: **4 ms** while the editor is active; **20 ms** while inactive (see "Editor-closed mode"). With a 2^18-frame ring this leaves >5000x margin even at 192 kHz.
  - Publish cadence: **16.67 ms** (60 Hz target, steady_clock-based, drift-corrected) while the editor is active and has fetched a snapshot in the last 500 ms; **none** when inactive (loudness/peak/stereo state keeps updating, nothing is built).
  - Thread priority: `Thread::Priority::low`-ish (`Thread::startThread(Priority::normal - 1)` equivalent; verify enum in JUCE 8.0.x at Stage 2). Worker sets FTZ/DAZ via `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` for its whole run loop.
  - **Deterministic core:** `AnalysisEngine::pump()` (drain+analyze) and `AnalysisEngine::buildSnapshot()` are plain methods; the worker only schedules them. Tests call them synchronously with no thread, so results do not depend on scheduling (this is also what guarantees block-size independence).
  - Shutdown: `signalThreadShouldExit()` + `stopThread(2000)` in `releaseResources()` and the processor destructor; editor never owns the worker.

### C4. Per-source StreamHistory
- **JUCE Class:** Custom ring (worker-private, no atomics)
- **Purpose:** Random-access history of the last 65536 frames per source (>= 16384 FFT + 4x gonio stride headroom + 8192 scope), filled by `drain()`. Provides `latest(n)` views (two contiguous segments) for FFT, scope and gonio extraction.
- **Configuration:** `float[2][65536]` per active source (0.5 MB). Tracks `framesSeen` (absolute stream index) so FFT hops and beat events are keyed to absolute sample indices.

### C5. Spectrum Engine
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::FFT` (module `juce_dsp`), `juce::dsp::WindowingFunction<float>` (hann, blackmanHarris) for table generation only
- **Purpose:** Windowed, coherent-gain-normalised magnitude spectrum, 75% overlap, mapped to 640 log-spaced dBFS points.
- **Parameters Affected:** `fft_size` (1024/2048/4096/8192/16384), `window` (hann/blackmanHarris), `analysis_mode`
- **Configuration:**
  - Five `juce::dsp::FFT` objects (orders 10..14) and 10 window tables (5 sizes x 2 windows) pre-created in `prepare`; a window change or size change is a table/pointer switch on the worker at the next hop (no re-allocation on the hot path). Scratch `float[2*16384]` per source.
  - Hop = N/4 (75% overlap), keyed to the absolute frame index so hop timing is independent of block size. FFT is executed on the **last N frames** of StreamHistory at each hop boundary. `hasSpectrum=false` until `framesSeen >= N` (honest "NO DATA").
  - Use `fft.performFrequencyOnlyForwardTransform(data, /*ignoreNegativeFreqs*/ true)` after applying the window (verify: JUCE writes magnitudes into the first N/2+1 entries; input buffer must be 2N floats).
  - **Coherent-gain normalisation:** `A_k = |X_k| * 2 / S`, `S = sum(w[n])` computed numerically from the actual table (Hann ~N/2, Blackman-Harris ~0.35875 N). DC and Nyquist bins use `1/S`. Result: a bin-centred sine of peak amplitude A reads exactly `20 log10(A)` dBFS (full-scale sine = 0 dBFS). Off-bin scalloping loss is up to 1.42 dB (Hann) / 0.83 dB (Blackman-Harris) and is documented, not corrected (a flat-top window is not in the spec's window list).
  - `analysis_mode` (see ambiguity A1): `combined` = per-bin **power mean** `(|L|^2+|R|^2)/2` (not the FFT of L+R, which would cancel anti-phase content); `leftRight` = the Left channel's spectrum; `midSide` = Mid spectrum with `M=(L+R)/sqrt2`. Mono sources always use the single channel. Both channel transforms (2 FFTs per source per hop; M/S built in the time domain then 1-2 FFTs) are executed only for the selected mode.
  - If multiple hops completed since the last publish (small N or high fs), the published curve is the **linear-power mean** of those frames (energy-calibrated, unbiased for noise; transients inside a window longer than the publish interval can't be missed because 75%-overlapped windows >= 1024 samples at <= 192 kHz still overlap each other; power-mean is chosen over max-hold to avoid inflating noise floors).
  - **Log mapping to 640 points** (matches v8: `f_i = 20 * 1000^(i/639)` Hz, i.e. 20 Hz..20 kHz, `OCTS = log2(1000)`): where bin spacing is finer than the point spacing (HF) use **max over the bins within the point's band edges** (`f_i * 2^(+-1/(2*639/9.966))`), which preserves sine calibration; where bins are coarser (LF) use **linear-in-dB interpolation** between the two nearest bins (smooth, does not invent energy: a measured curve is interpolated, never extrapolated). Bin->point index tables are precomputed per (fs, N) in `prepare`/size change. Points above Nyquist (fs < 40.1 kHz only) clamp to the floor.
  - Output floor **-120 dBFS** (clamp; zero input -> -120, never `-inf`). The UI's display floor is its own concern.
  - **Un-tilted, un-smoothed** (smoothing/attack-release, tilt, peak-hold are all UI-side per spec). The spectrogram uses the same 640 points (the v8 `spectrogram` frame field is optional and omitted by the editor).
- **Cost:** worst case 192 kHz, N=1024 -> hop 256 -> 750 hops/s x 2 sources x <=2 FFTs = 3000 FFT/s x ~3 us = ~1% of one core. N=16384, hop 4096 @192k: 47 hops/s x 4 FFT x ~150 us = ~3% of one core.

### C6. Loudness Engine (BS.1770-5 / EBU R128 / TECH 3342)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (`prism::LoudnessMeter`, `prism::KWeighting`). `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter` is NOT used: K-weighting needs **double-precision biquads** (38 Hz high-pass at 192 kHz in float loses accuracy) with coefficients derived analytically per sample rate.
- **Purpose:** Momentary (400 ms), short-term (3 s), integrated (gated), LRA.
- **Parameters Affected:** none (reset via `reset_all`, `reset_integrated`)
- **Configuration:**
  - **K-weighting** (two cascaded biquads per channel, bilinear transform of the analogue prototypes; same constants libebur128 uses, they reproduce the BS.1770 48 kHz table):
    - Stage 1, high shelf: `f0 = 1681.974450955533 Hz`, `G = 3.999843853973347 dB`, `Q = 0.7071752369554196`. `K=tan(pi f0/fs); Vh=10^(G/20); Vb=Vh^0.4996667741545416; a0=1+K/Q+K^2; b0=(Vh+Vb K/Q+K^2)/a0; b1=2(K^2-Vh)/a0; b2=(Vh-Vb K/Q+K^2)/a0; a1=2(K^2-1)/a0; a2=(1-K/Q+K^2)/a0`.
    - Stage 2, RLB high-pass: `f0 = 38.13547087602444 Hz`, `Q = 0.5003270373238773`. `K=tan(pi f0/fs); a0=1+K/Q+K^2; b=[1,-2,1]; a1=2(K^2-1)/a0; a2=(1-K/Q+K^2)/a0`.
    - **Fixture check at 48 kHz** (BS.1770 table): stage 1 `b=[1.53512485958697,-2.69169618940638,1.19839281085285]`, `a=[1,-1.69065929318241,0.73248077421585]`; stage 2 `a=[1,-1.99004745483398,0.99007225036621]`. A unit test asserts the derived coefficients match to 1e-9.
  - **Channel weights:** L = R = 1.0 (BS.1770-5 stereo; -5 only adds immersive-layout weights, irrelevant to v1). A mono source is measured as a single channel with weight 1.0 (a mono-on-stereo-bus track on L only reads 3 dB lower than the same signal on both channels - standard behavior).
  - **Chunking:** K-weighted mean-square accumulated in **10 ms chunks** (`chunk = round(0.01 fs)`; exact for 44.1/48/88.2/96/176.4/192 kHz). Ring of the last 300 chunk sums (per source): momentary = sum of last 40 chunks (updated every 10 ms), short-term = last 300. `LUFS = -0.691 + 10 log10(sum_c G_c * ms_c)`; mean-square below 1e-12 (< -120 LUFS) is published as **NaN** (dashes), see ambiguity A4.
  - **Gating blocks:** 400 ms, 75% overlap -> a new block every 10 chunks (100 ms), once >= 40 chunks exist. Each block's energy `z` goes into a **fine histogram** (0.01 LU bins from -70.0 to +10.0 LUFS = 8000 bins; per-bin `count` and `double energySum`): bounded memory regardless of session length (a plain block list grows 36 k/hour and needs allocation). Blocks below -70 LUFS are not stored.
  - **Integrated:** `Gamma_a = -70 LUFS`; `Gamma_r = -0.691 + 10 log10(mean energy of blocks > Gamma_a) - 10`; integrated = `-0.691 + 10 log10(mean energy of blocks > max(Gamma_a, Gamma_r))`. Recomputed from the histogram (O(8000)) only when a new gating block was added (10 Hz). NaN until at least one block passes both gates.
  - **LRA (EBU TECH 3342):** second histogram of **short-term (3 s) loudness values sampled every 100 ms** (libebur128 cadence; TECH 3342 permits >= 1 Hz); absolute gate -70 LUFS; relative gate = (power-mean of values above absolute gate) - **20 LU**; LRA = `L95 - L10` percentile difference of the gated distribution (histogram interpolation). NaN until at least one gated short-term value exists; 0.0 if the gated distribution collapses to a single bin.
  - **Which source feeds the snapshot:** the snapshot's `momentaryLufs/shortTermLufs/integratedLufs/loudnessRange` are global fields (v8 contract). v1 publishes **source 0 (main input)**. Loudness is *also computed* for the sidechain (cost: 2 biquad cascades x 2 ch, negligible) so a future `perSource loudness` extension needs no DSP change (see A2).
  - **Resets:** the processor exposes `requestResetAll()` / `requestResetIntegrated()` which increment `std::atomic<uint32_t>` epoch counters; the worker compares epochs each cycle (message thread never touches analyzer state). `reset_integrated` clears the gating histogram + LRA histogram; `reset_all` additionally clears max TP / max SP. (Spectrum peak-hold reset in `reset_all` is a UI-side operation in JS.) Momentary/short-term windows are *not* cleared by reset (they are moving windows).
  - **Gap handling:** after a ring overrun or sample-rate change the K-weighting filter state and the in-flight 400 ms block are discarded (one block dropped) rather than glitching; integrated state survives.

### C7. True-Peak + Sample-Peak Meters
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (`prism::TruePeakMeter`). `juce::dsp::Oversampling` is NOT used: its FIR/IIR latency-compensated structure is general-purpose, allocates per `prepare`, and its `processSamplesUp` writes full-block upsampled data (4x memory) - we need a streaming peak detector with the ITU-specified filter, not an oversampled audio path.
- **Purpose:** True peak per BS.1770-5 Annex 2 (oversampled; spec requires >= 4x), sample peak, both as "max since reset_all" in dB.
- **Parameters Affected:** none
- **Configuration:**
  - Streaming **4x polyphase FIR interpolator** (the Annex 2 reference filter: 48 taps = 4 phases x 12 taps, per channel), run on the worker over the drained frames. Output samples' absolute values are max-folded. **4x is used at every host sample rate** (including 88.2/96/176.4/192 kHz): this exceeds the standard at high rates (BS.1770-5 reportedly asks for an oversampled rate >= 192 kHz - *third-party summary, verify against the PDF*) and satisfies the contract's ">= 4x". Cost at 192 kHz: 2 sources x 2 ch x 192 k x 48 MAC = 37 MMAC/s (< 1% of a core).
  - `TP_dB = 20 log10(max over channels and sources' own channels)` -> `truePeakMaxDb`; **invariant enforced in the engine** (spec states it as a DSP invariant): `truePeakMax = max(truePeakMax, samplePeakMax)` so rounding in the interpolator can never read below the sample peak (Annex 2 phase 0 is not an exact unit impulse).
  - `samplePeakMaxDb` comes from the audio thread's lossless atomic (C2), drained by the worker with `exchange(0)` each cycle -> folded into the running max. True peak is computed from the ring data (a dropped block - an overrun - can lose a true-peak but never a sample-peak; overruns are surfaced in a debug counter).
  - Silence: max stays at its previous value; before any non-zero data, both are `-INFINITY` (-> `null` -> dashes) which matches the v8 default.
  - **dBTP accuracy note:** 4x oversampling can still under-read worst-case inter-sample peaks (up to ~0.69 dB for a tone at fs/2... only at 48 kHz-class rates for pathological phase). Documented limitation; EBU TECH 3341 tolerance for TP is +0.2/-0.4 dB.

### C8. Stereo Metrics (correlation / width / balance)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (`prism::StereoMetrics`)
- **Purpose:** Exactly the spec's *Meter Definitions* table.
- **Configuration:**
  - Running sums over a **400 ms rolling window** (40 x 10 ms buckets of `sum(l*r), sum(l^2), sum(r^2)` in `double`; ambiguity A3 - the spec says "the measurement window" without a duration).
  - `corr = Slr / sqrt(Sll*Srr)`; if `Sll*Srr < 1e-20` -> published `0` (spec: silence -> 0). Clamp to [-1, 1] after division to remove rounding overshoot.
  - `Em = sum((l+r)^2)/2`, `Es = sum((l-r)^2)/2` (i.e. `M=(L+R)/sqrt2`, `S=(L-R)/sqrt2`); `width = 100*sqrt(Es)/(sqrt(Es)+sqrt(Em))`; both zero -> 0. Mono -> 0, anti-phase -> 100, hard-panned -> 50 (verified analytically in tests). True 100 is emitted as 100.
  - `bal = 10 log10(Srr/Sll)`, both zero -> 0; one side zero and the other not -> clamp to +-60 dB (a finite honest "fully one-sided" value instead of +-inf which the bridge can't carry).
  - `hasStereo = (source.numChannels == 2)`; mono sources publish `hasStereo=false` (-> `null`, dashes).
  - All sums are in double; no mean removal (spec: "non-mean-removed").

### C9. Scope + Goniometer Capture
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (copies from StreamHistory)
- **Purpose:** Time-domain window and L/R pairs for the oscilloscope and vectorscope.
- **Configuration:**
  - **Scope:** per source, one channel: `leftRight` -> L; `midSide` -> M (=(L+R)/sqrt2 limited to [-1,1] only by display, raw values published); `combined` -> (L+R)/2 (ambiguity A1/A5). `scopeCount = min(kScopeSamples, ceil(0.020*fs) + 800 + 256)` -> 1,760 at 48 kHz, 4,896 at 192 kHz (<= 8192 contract). Sending only what the UI can use cuts bridge bandwidth ~4x versus always sending 8192. **Trigger support:** v8's JS performs the rising-zero search inside the +800 sample slack (contract: "scope window >= 20 ms + 800 samples"); the engine contract is "the most recent `scopeCount` contiguous frames". An optional engine-side trigger alignment (find last rising zero crossing, shift the window) is deliberately *not* in v1 because it would double-trigger with the UI search; a note in plan.md lists it as a v1.1 upgrade if scope jitter is objectionable.
  - **Gonio:** last `900 * stride` frames sampled every `stride = max(1, round(3 * fs/48000))` frame -> 900 L/R pairs spanning ~56 ms at any sample rate (matches the v8 mockup's "900 samples/frame at stride 3" at 48 kHz and keeps the persistence look consistent across rates). Raw L/R in [-1, 1] (mono: L=R, giving the vertical mono line); `S=(R-L)/sqrt2` mapping is applied in JS per the spec's vectorscope convention.

### C10. Band Energy / Waveform Column Extractor
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::LinkwitzRileyFilter<float>` (module `juce_dsp`) x2 per source (verify `setType(lowpass/highpass)` and `processSample(channel, x)` usage at Stage 2); or equivalently two custom LR4 biquad pairs
- **Purpose:** Rekordbox-style 3-band waveform columns: `[bass, mids, highs, flag]`, 84.33 columns/s (12 s window = 1012 px / 12 s, from the v8 UI).
- **Parameters Affected:** none (UI selects Ch1/Ch2)
- **Configuration:**
  - Input per source = mono sum `(L+R)/2` (ambiguity A5 - the UI has one column stream per source). Crossovers: LR4 at **200 Hz** and **2.5 kHz** (tunable constants): `low = LP200(x)`, `rest = HP200(x)`, `mid = LP2500(rest)`, `high = HP2500(rest)`. Phase compensation is unnecessary (energy only).
  - Column period `Tc = fs / 84.33` samples (fractional accumulator; no drift). Per column and band: **peak** of `|band|` over the column's samples, mapped `v = clamp((20 log10(peak) + 54)/54, 0, 1)` (a -54 dBFS..0 dBFS window; documented tuning constant - the UI already scales mids x0.8 and highs x0.52 so absolute 0..1 meaning is "relative strength").
  - `flag`: beat/bar markers from the audio thread's BeatEventQueue (C2): a marker whose absolute frame index falls inside the column sets `1` (beat) or `2` (bar, overrides 1). No host transport -> flags 0 (the UI still scrolls).
  - Snapshot carries only the **new** columns (<= `kMaxWaveformColumns = 16`). **Consumer-acknowledged accumulation** (see Threading): columns are retained in a worker-side column log (4096 entries) and every snapshot contains all columns newer than the last one the editor *actually fetched*, so a skipped publish never creates a visible gap. If more than 16 are pending (UI stalled > 190 ms) the oldest are dropped and a `waveformGap` condition is simply visible as a jump (honest).
  - BPM: `snapshot.bpm = atomic bpm` (NaN absent).

### C11. Snapshot Publisher / Mailbox
- **JUCE Class:** `std::shared_ptr<const prism::AnalysisSnapshot>`, `juce::SpinLock` (guards only a pointer swap/copy between the **worker and message threads - never the audio thread**)
- **Purpose:** Race-free ownership of immutable snapshots.
- **Configuration:**
  - `Mailbox::publish(std::shared_ptr<const Snapshot>)` (worker) and `Mailbox::fetch()` (message thread) each do `{ SpinLock::ScopedLockType l(lock); ptr = ...; }` - two pointer copies under a ~10 ns critical section. **Chosen over `std::atomic<std::shared_ptr>`** because Apple libc++ support for `atomic<shared_ptr>` is recent and not uniform across the factory's toolchains; the deprecated `std::atomic_load(shared_ptr*)` free functions are also avoided. The v8 editor's comment ("std::atomic_load on a shared_ptr") is satisfied by `processor.getLatestAnalysisSnapshot()` hiding this.
  - Each snapshot is `std::make_shared<AnalysisSnapshot>()` on the worker (~90 KB; 60 allocations/s; worker thread only - allowed). Optional Stage-2 optimisation: 4-slot recycle pool with a custom deleter if allocator profiling shows pressure.
  - `getLatestAnalysisSnapshot()` also stores `lastFetchedSequence` and `lastFetchTimeMs` in atomics (editor-activity + column acknowledgement).

---

## Processing Chain

```
HOST AUDIO (main bus in == main bus out, in-place; sidechain bus in)
        |
  processBlock()   [AUDIO THREAD - wait-free, no alloc, no lock, writes NOTHING to audio]
     |-- ScopedNoDenormals
     |-- per source s: blockPeak -> atomic fetch_max(samplePeak[s])
     |-- per source s: memcpy L/R -> SpscFrameRing[s]   (drop block + overrunCount++ if full)
     |-- playhead: bpm -> atomic;  beat/bar boundary -> BeatEventQueue
     '-- (output buffer untouched => bit-exact passthrough, 0 latency)

        SPSC rings (lock-free)
              |
  AnalysisWorker  [WORKER THREAD, normal-1 priority, FTZ/DAZ]  poll 4 ms (editor active) / 20 ms (inactive)
     |-- drain ring -> StreamHistory[s]                    (sanitize non-finite -> 0, count them)
     |-- ALWAYS (even editor closed):  K-weight biquads -> 10 ms chunk sums
     |                                  -> M / S / gating blocks -> integrated, LRA histograms
     |                                  4x polyphase true peak, sample-peak fold
     |                                  400 ms rolling corr/width/balance sums
     |-- EDITOR ACTIVE only:           FFT hops (N/4) -> power-mean -> 640 log pts (dBFS)
     |                                  LR4 3-band split -> waveform columns @ 84.33/s (+ beat flags)
     |                                  scope window, gonio pairs
     '-- every 16.67 ms (active): build immutable AnalysisSnapshot -> Mailbox.publish()

        Mailbox (SpinLock-guarded shared_ptr<const Snapshot>)
              |
  Editor timer 60 Hz  [MESSAGE THREAD]  fetchLatestSnapshot() -> skip if sequence == lastSequence
     '-- pack floats (base64) -> webView->emitEventIfBrowserIsVisible("prismFrame", ...)
              |
  WebView JS  receiveAnalysisFrame(frame)   (smoothing, tilt, peak-hold, themes = UI-side)
```

**Routing notes**
- No parallel audio paths; no feedback loops; no audio-domain DSP. All "processing" is analysis.
- Source 1 (sidechain) may be absent (bus disabled, Standalone, host without sidechain): it simply stays `active=false` -> `hasSpectrum=false`, `hasStereo=false`, no gonio/scope, peaks `-INF`, and the UI shows dashes / "No data". Never zeros-as-data.
- `freeze` is a UI-only display freeze; the engine keeps running so integrated loudness and peaks are never lost.

---

## System Architecture

### File I/O System
Not applicable (no file I/O). The v2 PRISM Sender IPC directory is reserved but unimplemented.

### Multi-Output Routing / Bus Layout (applicable)

**Bus configuration:**
```cpp
PRISMAudioProcessor::PRISMAudioProcessor()
  : AudioProcessor (BusesProperties()
        .withInput  ("Input",     juce::AudioChannelSet::stereo(), true)
        .withOutput ("Output",    juce::AudioChannelSet::stereo(), true)
        .withInput  ("Sidechain", juce::AudioChannelSet::stereo(), false)),   // optional, off by default
```
- **CRITICAL:** `BusesProperties` is built in the constructor (juce8-critical-patterns #4), never in `prepareToPlay`.
- `isBusesLayoutSupported(layouts)`:
  1. `layouts.getMainOutputChannelSet() == layouts.getMainInputChannelSet()` (bit-exact in-place passthrough requires identical in/out).
  2. Main set is `mono()` or `stereo()` (non-empty, never disabled).
  3. Sidechain input (bus index 1 of inputs): `disabled()`, `mono()` or `stereo()`.
  4. Reject everything else (surround/ambisonics) - honest failure beats mis-measurement in v1.
- `processBlock` obtains views with `getBusBuffer(buffer, true, 0)` and `getBusBuffer(buffer, true, 1)` (only if `getBus(true,1)->isEnabled()`); these are **read-only** views; the host's shared buffer is `max(totalIn, totalOut)` channels, and the sidechain occupies channels after the main bus.
- **Scaling to 8-16 sources:** additional `withInput("Source N", stereo, false)` entries (added only when the target host supports it) map to source indices by bus order. `SourceRegistry` and per-source analyzers are indexed, `kMaxSources=16`; `kSourceCount` (snapshot arrays, bridge arrays, UI) stays 2 until v1.x/v2 lifts it. The snapshot struct is the only place that needs resizing (then ~45 KB x 16 = 0.7 MB per snapshot, which argues for sparse-source publication at that point; deferred).
- **DAW notes:** Ableton Live 12: sidechain routing = "Audio From" chooser on the plugin's sidechain input (VST3 and AU). Logic: AU sidechain popup. Reaper/Bitwig/Cubase: full multibus, only the first extra bus used in v1. FL Studio: sidechain to a second bus works for VST3 via routing. Standalone: no sidechain device -> source 2 inactive. Fallback when the host refuses the optional bus: engine runs single-source and the UI shows Ch2 as no-data.

### MIDI Routing
None. `acceptsMidi=false`, `producesMidi=false`, `isMidiEffect=false`. Host tempo/transport come only through `AudioPlayHead`.

### State Persistence

**What is saved (all inside `apvts.state` -> one XML blob):**
- 17 APVTS parameters (automatic).
- ValueTree properties: `src1_name`, `src2_name` (<= 10 chars; empty -> default), `ui_row_splits`, `ui_lower_col_splits`, `ui_spectrogram_orientation`, `ui_fullscreen`, `ui_width`, `ui_height`.
- **Not saved (runtime-only):** loudness histograms, peak maxima, FFT history. A project reload never "confuses" instances because nothing about analysis is persisted; each instance starts clean (integrated loudness restarts - documented; this is also the honest behavior since the audio before reload isn't available).

**Serialization:** `getStateInformation`: `auto xml = apvts.copyState().createXml(); copyXmlToBinary(*xml, dest)`. `setStateInformation`: parse, verify tag name == `apvts.state.getType()`, run **sanitizer** (clamp splits to minimums and fixed totals 598/834, enum strings validated, name length, window size to aspect 55:36 min 770x504) *before* `apvts.replaceState(...)` so a corrupt state never reaches the editor.
**Restore behavior:** invalid XML -> keep defaults; unknown/future properties preserved but ignored; parameter versioning `juce::ParameterID{id, 1}`.
**Editor sync:** the existing `ParamBridge`/`valueTreeRedirected` path re-pushes `prismInit` (already in v8 scaffolding).

### Preset / Bridge semantics (engine-side)
`preset` is a pure choice parameter with **no engine effect**: C++ must NOT apply the bundle (spec). `prismParam` gesture handling lives entirely in the editor (v8 scaffolding).

## Parameter Mapping

All 17 ids verbatim from `parameter-spec.md`, in spec order. "Engine" = analysis behavior; "UI" = forwarded to JS only (engine ignores; present in APVTS for host automation/persistence).

| Parameter ID | Type | Range / Default | Component | Engine behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fft_size` | Choice | 1024/2048/4096/8192/16384, def 4096 | C5 Spectrum | Selects FFT order 10..14 and hop N/4; takes effect at the next hop. Also drives the log-map index tables and `hasSpectrum` warm-up. |
| `window` | Choice | hann/blackmanHarris, def hann | C5 Spectrum | Selects window table + its `S=sum(w)` normaliser. |
| `smoothing` | Float | 0-100 %, def 35 | UI | None (display-side attack 5+0.6v ms / release 30+8v ms). Snapshot is unsmoothed. |
| `spectrum_tilt` | Float | 0-4.5 dB/oct, def 0 | UI | None. Engine data stays untilted; spectrogram/inspector are true dBFS. |
| `display_range` | Choice | -48/-60/-72/-90, def -90 | UI | None. Engine floor is a fixed -120 dBFS so range changes never need re-analysis. |
| `spectrogram_speed` | Float | 0.25-4.0x log, def 1.0 | UI | None. Needs custom `NormalisableRange` (`convertFrom0to1 = min*pow(max/min, n)`, inverse via `log`) with 0.01 interval - Stage 1 task. |
| `peak_decay` | Float | 3-60 dB/s, def 12 | UI | None (UI peak-hold after 1.2 s). |
| `freeze` | Bool | def off | UI | None. Engine keeps measuring. |
| `analysis_mode` | Choice | leftRight/midSide/combined, def combined | C5, C9 | Channel domain for spectrum curve (and, for consistency, scope channel). Loudness/peaks/stereo metrics are *always* L/R-based (unaffected). |
| `color_theme` | Choice | 7, def `Coral/Mint` | UI | None (strings verbatim incl. slash; Stage 1 choice list must match exactly). |
| `preset` | Choice | 6, def Studio | UI | None; C++ never applies bundles. |
| `reduced_motion` | Bool | def off | UI (+ optional) | Editor MAY halve the `prismFrame` push rate to 30 Hz when set (spec: "halves the render rate"); engine unaffected. |
| `glow_intensity` | Float | 0-100 %, def 55 | UI | None. |
| `src1_visible` | Bool | def on | UI | None (analysis stays on for hidden sources). |
| `src1_solo` | Bool | def off | UI | None. |
| `src2_visible` | Bool | def on | UI | None. |
| `src2_solo` | Bool | def off | UI | None. |

State entries `src1_name`/`src2_name`: ValueTree strings, no engine role.
Momentary actions `reset_all` / `reset_integrated`: not parameters; routed `editor -> processor.requestResetAll()/requestResetIntegrated()` -> epoch atomics -> worker (C6).

Only 3 parameters (`fft_size`, `window`, `analysis_mode`) are read by the worker; `reduced_motion` is optionally read by the editor timer. The worker reads them via `apvts.getRawParameterValue(id)->load()` once per cycle (atomic, RT-safe, no listener needed).

## Data Structures: AnalysisSnapshot layout vs `prismFrame`

The v8 struct in `v8-PluginEditor.h` moves **verbatim** to `Source/Analysis/AnalysisSnapshot.h` (keeping the `PRISM_ANALYSIS_SNAPSHOT_DEFINED` guard). Do not change field names/sizes. Constants: `kSourceCount=2`, `kSpectrumPoints=640`, `kMaxWaveformColumns=16`, `kGonioPairs=900`, `kScopeSamples=8192`.

| Snapshot field | Producer | `prismFrame` JSON | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence` | worker, ++ per publish (strictly increasing, starts 1) | (editor skip key) | |
| `sampleRate` | engine `fs` | `sampleRate` | |
| `bpm` | audio-thread atomic | `bpm` / null | |
| `signalPresent` | any active source's block peak > -90 dBFS within the last 500 ms | `live` | else UI "NO SIGNAL" |
| `momentaryLufs` / `shortTermLufs` / `integratedLufs` / `loudnessRange` | C6 source 0 | `meters.loudness.{M,S,I,LRA}` | NaN -> null |
| `sources[i].hasSpectrum`, `spectrumDb[640]` | C5 | `spectrum[i]` (base64 f32) | dBFS true/un-tilted, floor -120 |
| `sources[i].waveformColumnCount`, `waveformColumns[<=16][4]` | C10 | `waveform[i]` (flat x4) | bass, mids, highs 0..1, flag 0/1/2 |
| `sources[i].gonioPairCount`, `gonio[1800]` | C9 | `gonio[i]` | interleaved L,R |
| `sources[i].scopeCount`, `scope[8192]` | C9 | `scope[i]` | count <= 8192, typ. 1.8k-4.9k |
| `truePeakMaxDb`, `samplePeakMaxDb` | C7 | `meters.peaks[i].{tp,sp}` | -INF -> null |
| `hasStereo`, `correlation`, `widthPercent`, `balanceDb` | C8 | `meters.stereo[i]` / null | |

Size: each `SourceSnapshot` ~ (640 + 64 + 1800 + 8192 + 6) x 4 B = ~43 KB, snapshot ~87 KB. `std::array` members are zero-initialised by `make_shared`; the worker fills only the used prefix (counts convey length).

**Bridge bandwidth (60 Hz):** 48 kHz: spectrum 2x2.5 KB + gonio 2x7.2 KB + scope 2x7 KB + misc = ~34 KB raw / ~46 KB base64 per frame = 2.8 MB/s. 192 kHz: scope 2x19.6 KB -> ~80 KB base64 = 4.8 MB/s. Acceptable for `evaluateJavascript`-based event delivery but is the primary Stage-3 performance risk (see Risks).

## Algorithm Details

### Block-size independence and arbitrary rates
- The audio thread only appends samples; **every** time-based quantity (FFT hops, 10 ms loudness chunks, 400 ms stereo window, 84.33 col/s, beat markers) is keyed to the **absolute frame index** in the worker. Nothing depends on `getNumSamples()`. Verified by tests that render the same stream with block sizes {1, 7, 64, 480, 4096} and compare snapshots bit-for-bit (after synchronous `pump()`).
- Supported rates: 44.1/48/88.2/96/176.4/192 kHz are first-class (integer chunk sizes). Other rates (22.05..384 kHz) work with rounded chunk sizes (< 0.05 % timing error). `prepareToPlay` with an unchanged `{fs, layout}` does **not** reset analysis (hosts call it repeatedly); a changed rate/layout rebuilds all analyzers (and clears integrated state - documented).
- `kScopeSamples=8192` covers the scope's `0.02*fs+800+256` need up to 352.8 kHz (7,856+256 > 8,192 only above ~370 kHz; clamped in code).

### Silence, transport, suspension, editor closed
- **Silence** (digital zero): spectrum -120 dBFS, correlation 0, balance 0, width 0 (per spec), loudness NaN when below -120 LUFS else real value, `signalPresent=false`. Peaks hold. Gated integrated loudness correctly ignores blocks below -70 LUFS.
- **Transport stop:** hosts keep calling `processBlock` with silence (or stop calling it). If calls stop, the worker sees no new frames, no new `sequence` is produced, the editor idles and the JS side shows "NO DATA" after 1 s. Resuming continues seamlessly (rings are not reset). A gap longer than one ring (no calls) needs no handling; stale data is simply not re-published (publishing only happens when new frames arrived since the last publish *or* meters changed).
- **Suspension / `releaseResources()`:** stop the worker; `prepareToPlay()` restarts it (reusing analyzers if `{fs, layout}` unchanged).
- **Editor-closed CPU minimisation:** the editor sets `processor.setEditorActive(true/false)` in ctor/dtor (atomic counter), and the mailbox fetch timestamp doubles as a "view visible/alive" heartbeat (hidden WebView still has its timer running; `emitEventIfBrowserIsVisible` drops the push but the fetch continues - see Risks R6). When inactive: no FFT, no band split, no scope/gonio, no snapshot build; the always-on set is 2 biquad cascades + gating + true-peak + corr sums = ~0.3% of a core at 48 kHz/2 sources, 20 ms poll.
- **Non-finite input** (NaN/Inf from a misbehaving upstream plugin): counted (`nonFiniteCount`), replaced by 0 in the worker copy, never propagated to meters, never alters the audio path. Audio is not touched.
- **Denormals:** `ScopedNoDenormals` on both threads; biquad state in double with a 1e-30 DC-guard flush in the reset path; FFT inputs windowed floats are not denormal-prone after the `-120 dB` clamp.

### Latency
Exactly 0 samples; `getLatencySamples()` = 0, `getTailLengthSeconds()` = 0.

---

## Integration Points

### Feature Dependencies
- Capture ring (C2) -> everything: all analyzers consume the worker's StreamHistory; no analyzer touches audio-thread memory.
- StreamHistory (C4) -> FFT (C5), scope/gonio (C9), band extractor (C10).
- K-weighting (C6) -> chunk sums -> momentary/short-term -> gating histogram -> integrated -> LRA (LRA reuses the short-term series).
- True-peak (C7) <- audio-thread lossless sample-peak atomic (SP) for the invariant `TP >= SP`.
- Beat events (audio thread, C2) -> column flags (C10) -> `waveformColumns[].flag` -> waveform strip beat ticks.
- Mailbox (C11) <- everything above; editor timer consumes.
- `reset_*` events -> epoch atomics -> C6/C7.

### Parameter Interactions
- `fft_size` x sample rate: frequency resolution `fs/N`, `hasSpectrum` warm-up time `N/fs` (up to 340 ms at 44.1 kHz/16384); the 640-point map must be rebuilt at size change (index tables).
- `window` changes the normaliser `S`; must be applied atomically with the window table (the same pointer switch) so a frame never mixes table A with normaliser B.
- `analysis_mode` x mono source: mono forces single-channel regardless of mode.
- `src*_visible/solo` never alter the engine - hidden sources keep accumulating loudness/peaks (so toggling visibility doesn't discard measurements).
- `reduced_motion` x publish rate (optional editor-side 30 Hz) - the engine's column accumulation (acknowledgement scheme) guarantees no waveform gaps at any editor push rate.
- `spectrum_tilt`/`display_range` do not alter the engine; spectrogram intensity must not change with tilt (JS honors it - spec).

### Processing Order
1. (audio) peaks + ring write; 2. (worker) drain; 3. K-weight+chunks; 4. gating/histograms; 5. TP/SP fold; 6. stereo sums; 7. FFT hops; 8. band columns; 9. scope/gonio extraction; 10. build+publish snapshot. Steps 7-9 are skipped when the editor is inactive.

### Thread Boundaries
| Boundary | Mechanism | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Audio -> Worker | `SpscFrameRing` (acquire/release atomics), `BeatEventQueue`, atomics (`samplePeak`, `bpm`, `overrunCount`, `nonFiniteCount`) | audio thread wait-free; drop-on-full, never block |
| Worker -> Message | `Mailbox` (SpinLock-guarded `shared_ptr<const Snapshot>`) + `lastFetchedSequence` ack atomic | snapshot immutable after publish; reader holds a refcount, never blocks the worker beyond ~10 ns |
| Message -> Worker | `std::atomic<uint32_t>` reset epochs, `editorActive` counter, raw APVTS param atomics | polled each worker cycle |
| Message <-> WebView | v8 `ParamBridge` + `emitEventIfBrowserIsVisible` | already scaffolded |
| Message -> Audio | none | (APVTS parameters are not read in processBlock) |

**Consumer-acknowledged waveform accumulation:** each published snapshot records the highest column index it contains; `getLatestAnalysisSnapshot()` writes `lastFetchedSequence`; the worker maps sequence -> highest column in a 64-entry ring and starts the next snapshot's columns at `ackedColumn+1`. If a snapshot is published but never fetched (editor busy), its columns are re-sent in the next one (up to the 16-column cap).

| R1 | Host sidechain availability (Live VST3/AU, Standalone, hosts that refuse optional buses) | MEDIUM | HIGH | Sidechain bus is optional/disabled-by-default; engine tolerates `active=false`; UI shows no-data honestly. **Fallback:** ship main-only + documented "enable sidechain input in host" instructions; keep `isBusesLayoutSupported` permissive (disabled sidechain always legal). Test matrix: Live 12 VST3+AU, Logic AU, Reaper VST3, Standalone, `pluginval` strictness 5 (it exercises bus layouts). |
| R2 | WebView 60 fps frame delivery (4.8 MB/s base64 at 192 kHz; JSON serialization on the message thread; WKWebView/WebView2 evaluateJavascript cost) | MEDIUM-HIGH | HIGH | Measure in Stage 3 Phase 3.3. Levers in order: (1) trim scope to the needed length (already), (2) send gonio/scope at 30 Hz, spectrum+meters at 60 Hz (per-field decimation in `pushAnalysisFrame`), (3) halve rate under `reduced_motion`, (4) lower gonio to 600 pairs, (5) **fallback:** binary delivery via the resource provider (a `/frame.bin` fetch polled by JS) or `juce::var` `MemoryBlock` transfer if the JUCE 8 version supports it - to be spiked only if (1)-(4) miss budget. | R3 | Worker scheduling / thread starvation (loaded DAW, power-saving cores) | MEDIUM | MEDIUM | 2^18-frame ring (>=1.37 s at 192 kHz) - tolerates ~1 s stalls; sample peak lossless via atomic; overrun is detected, loudness block dropped, never fabricated. Priority below normal; `Thread::wait` with timeout; deterministic `pump()` catches up in one pass. **Fallback:** raise priority one notch, ring to 2^19. |
| R4 | 192 kHz CPU load | LOW-MEDIUM | MEDIUM | Estimated < 8% of one core, editor open, worst case (N=16384 + 1024 combos, 2 sources, 4x TP). Profiling gate in plan (Phase 2.7). Levers: TP 2x at >=88.2 kHz (still >=192 kHz oversampled), skip LRA histogram hist-update to 1 Hz, FFT of M/S only when selected. |

| R6 | Hidden editor still fetching snapshots (host hides plugin window but editor object lives) -> wasted worker CPU | LOW | LOW | Activity heartbeat = last fetch time; editor already uses `emitEventIfBrowserIsVisible` and stops consuming when hidden (v8). Add `processor.setEditorVisible(bool)` from `visibilityChanged` so the worker drops to inactive mode. |
| R7 | True-peak under-read vs reference meters | LOW | LOW | Use the Annex 2 FIR with the published coefficients (4 x 12 taps); verify with fs/4 sine at 45 deg (TP must read ~0 dBTP when SP reads -3.01) and TECH 3341 TP cases. **Fallback:** 8x with a longer windowed-sinc if tolerance is violated. |

| R10 | `juce::dsp::LinkwitzRileyFilter` API/behavior drift | LOW | LOW | Verify at Stage 2 start; fallback = 8 custom biquads (trivial). |

## Architecture Decisions

1. **One worker thread, deterministic engine core.** Alternatives: per-source threads (rejected: 2 sources are ~5% of a core; thread count scales badly toward 16 sources), analysis inside `processBlock` (rejected by the brief), `juce::TimeSliceThread` (viable, but a plain `juce::Thread` with poll gives simpler start/stop and no per-client scheduling jitter). Core logic callable synchronously -> unit-testable without threads.
2. **Everything but a memcpy and a max off the audio thread**, including true peak. Trade-off: TP is not computed inside the block but from the ring (<= 4 ms late; ring overrun can drop a TP window - sample peak stays lossless via the atomic). Chosen to keep `processBlock` cost ~constant and trivially provable RT-safe.
3. **Custom SPSC ring over `juce::AbstractFifo`:** variable-length contiguous frame copies and bounded drop policy with counters, no 2-region wrap logic duplicated in each caller.
4. **Immutable snapshots via SpinLock-guarded `shared_ptr`:** avoids `atomic<shared_ptr>` portability; contention is worker<->message only.
5. **Custom K-weighting in double, histogram gating:** `juce::dsp::IIR` is float-oriented and the 38 Hz stage is numerically fragile at 192 kHz; histogram gating bounds memory for multi-hour sessions.
6. **Custom 4x polyphase true-peak, not `juce::dsp::Oversampling`:** purpose-built streaming peak detector; used at all rates to satisfy ">= 4x".
7. **Spectrum calibrated in dBFS-per-sine (coherent gain), bin mapping = max (HF) / dB-interp (LF):** the visual spectrum is the same data the inspector reports (true dBFS); smoothing/tilt are display transforms only.
8. **Unsmoothed data, display-side smoothing:** keeps measurements honest and allows `smoothing`/`display_range` changes with zero engine work.
9. **Consumer-acknowledged waveform columns** instead of "latest only" frames: guarantees gapless waveform even if the WebView drops frames.
10. **Passthrough proof by construction:** the processor holds no write path to the buffer (read-only views, no `clear()`), and a bit-exactness test enforces it.

---

## Special Considerations

- **Thread safety:** see Thread Boundaries. Worker owns all analyzer state; message thread never touches it (resets via epochs). TSAN clean required.
- **Performance targets:** `processBlock` < 0.5% of block time at 64-sample buffers (two memcpys + one max scan); worker < 3% of a core at 48 kHz with the editor open, < 8% at 192 kHz; editor-closed < 0.5%.
- **Denormals:** see Silence section (both threads, double biquads).
- **Sample rate:** 44.1-192 kHz first-class; rebuild on change; FFT bin tables, K-weighting coefficients, crossover coefficients, chunk size, column period all recomputed in `prepare`.
- **Latency:** 0.
- **Memory:** per active source ~2.0 MB ring + 0.5 MB history + ~0.13 MB scratch/histograms + ~90 KB snapshot => ~6 MB total for v1; ~45 MB at 16 sources.
- **Accuracy honesty:** NaN/-INF are the only "unavailable" encodings; the engine never emits placeholder numbers. `overrunCount`/`nonFiniteCount` exposed to a debug log.
- **Logging/debug:** a `PRISM_DEBUG_STATS` build flag exposes counters (overruns, worker cycle ms) to a footer debug line; absent in release.

- EBU R128 and EBU TECH 3341 (metering), TECH 3342 (LRA), TECH 3343/3344 (guidance), including the compliance signal set used for fixtures.
- libebur128 (K-weighting constants, histogram gating, LRA cadence) and pyloudnorm - used as offline golden-value generators and algorithmic cross-check only; no code copied.
- Harris, "On the use of windows for harmonic analysis with the DFT" (coherent gain / scalloping figures).

## Validation / Test Strategy (summary; detail in plan.md)

Console harness `PRISM_Tests` (`setPlayConfigDetails` before `prepareToPlay` - factory note), driving `AnalysisEngine::pump()/buildSnapshot()` synchronously plus an end-to-end `processBlock` pass:
- FFT: bin-centred sines at -0.1/-20/-60 dBFS (+-0.1 dB), off-bin sines (+-1.5 dB Hann / +-1.0 dB BH), white noise level vs analytical per-bin density, impulse (flat spectrum), multitone (all tones within tolerance, freq error <= bin/2), each fft_size x window x fs {44.1, 48, 96, 192 kHz}.
- Loudness: coefficient fixture; 997 Hz sine references; EBU TECH 3341/3342 compliance cases; golden values from libebur128/pyloudnorm; gating (absolute/relative) synthetic step signals; reset semantics.
- True peak: fs/4 @ 45 deg sine, TECH 3341 TP cases, TP >= SP invariant, all rates.
- Stereo: identical -> corr +1/width 0/bal 0; inverted -> -1/100; independent noise -> ~0 (+-0.05); hard-left -> bal -60 (clamped)/width 50; silence -> 0.
- Passthrough bit-exactness (incl. NaN, denormals, sidechain on/off), zero allocations in `processBlock`, block-size independence, sample-rate change, TSAN stress.

---

## 12. Open Questions / Contract Ambiguities (decisions made here; flag if you disagree)

| ID | Ambiguity | Decision in this architecture |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | `analysis_mode` leftRight/midSide/combined, but the snapshot carries ONE spectrum curve per source | `combined` = power-mean of L and R; `leftRight` = Left channel; `midSide` = Mid. Both channel spectra could be computed so a future 2-curve-per-source layout needs no DSP change. Needs product confirmation (a cleaner UX may be L/R as two curves per source - requires a UI/contract change). |
| A2 | `AnalysisSnapshot` loudness fields are global (not per source) | Publish source 0 (main input). Sidechain loudness is computed but unpublished. |
| A3 | "Measurement window" for correlation/width/balance is unspecified | 400 ms rolling (same as momentary). |
| A4 | How to publish loudness for digital silence / below -120 LUFS | NaN (dashes). Integrated and LRA keep their gated values. |
| A5 | Scope/waveform/gonio channel for a stereo source (one array per source) | Scope follows `analysis_mode` (L / M / (L+R)/2); waveform bands use (L+R)/2; gonio keeps both channels. |
| A6 | Waveform 0..1 mapping and crossover frequencies unspecified | -54..0 dB peak window, LR4 at 200 Hz / 2.5 kHz (tunable constants). |
| A7 | Scope trigger: brief says "scope capture with trigger support"; v8 JS already does the rising-zero search | Engine supplies the window + 800-sample slack; no engine-side trigger in v1. |
| A8 | Contract says true peak ">= 4x"; BS.1770-5 Annex 2 reportedly asks >= 192 kHz effective (4x@48k, 2x@96k, 1x@192k) | 4x at every rate (superset of both). Verify against the PDF. |
| A9 | `spec` says "Parameters are implemented in EXACT order"; it also mentions "v7 said 21 params" | Treated as resolved: 17 APVTS + 2 state entries. |
| A10 | `display_range` choice order | Choice strings/indices exactly as parameter-spec.md (index 0 = `-48` ... 3 = `-90`, default index 3); the APVTS choice index must not be confused with the numeric dB value on the bridge. |
